note: Bill's weekly queue (Empire HQ, riftcompare.com/admin/hq). One row per step that needs Bill's hands. PUBLIC FILE: a title, a reason and the project-files path of the prompt only; never a key, a token, an address or a private name. Add a row and commit to main (no deploy needed: HQ reads this file from GitHub). Set done to the day you verified it, or Bill presses Done on HQ. The prompt text itself stays in project files; each Monday the steps still open are joined into one Chrome batch, chrome-queue/<date>.md.

steps.title: Finish the Compare Empire Bluesky account: app password into GitHub (one time; it then posts itself)
steps.why: The daily Bluesky job is built and dry-running: two link cards a day across all 13 sites, no recurring work, once the account exists.

steps.title: Turn off CamCompare's Vercel bot challenge again
steps.why: Since about 2 Nov it answers non-browser clients with 429 (fixed 30 Oct, back again): it blocks link previews, IndexNow and the Bluesky poster's CamCompare cards.

steps.title: Create the free Compare Empire GitHub organization (moves nothing)
steps.why: Step 1 of the approved consolidation plan: shared secrets and one place for every repo.

steps.title: BandaiCompare: domain, Vercel project, Cyberpunk's eBay keys as repo secrets, Amazon AU tracking ID bandaicompare-22, Search Console
steps.why: The site is built and importing; it earns nothing until the eBay secrets, the Amazon tag and the domain exist (owner, 3 Nov: share Cyberpunk Compare's eBay app at 2,500 calls a day).

steps.title: Cyberpunk Compare: add the site to Google Search Console (eBay keys and domain already done)
steps.why: The site and its own eBay keys are live since 2 Nov; Google still needs the property and sitemap.

steps.title: Amazon in one sitting: tracking IDs for Dex, MTG and OP, then join UK, Canada and Germany
steps.why: UK, CA and EU visitors see no Amazon link today, and Dex/MTG/OP sales count under RiftCompare's tag; every site's code is already wired.

steps.title: Bring www.compareempire.com back as a redirect (Vercel domain + one DNS record), then tidy Search Console
steps.why: www has had no DNS since 26 Oct and Google still files most pages under www; impressions fell from about 25K a day to about 200.

steps.title: Vercel: spend alerts at $170 a month, Standard build machines, scraper-bot firewall rule on every project
steps.why: 1 November cost $11.82 against a $5-6 a day ceiling; the code side (one build per 12 hours, no previews) is merged, these are dashboard-only.

steps.title: Switch on the Discord price bot: create the app, paste three values (one time, about 10 minutes)
steps.why: Growth plan 2026-11-03: the bot's answers and /daily game posts are seen by whole channels, a loop that brings new players without us posting. Everything after these 10 minutes runs itself (daily setup job).

steps.title: Vercel: turn on Web Analytics for wargamecompare and figurecompare (one Chrome prompt checks every project)
steps.why: Without it those two sites have no visitor counts on HQ. Every repo already mounts @vercel/analytics (checked 2026-11-03); only the dashboard toggle is left.

steps.title: Vercel: redirect ygocompare.app to ygocompare.com (Domains settings)
steps.why: Two hosts split Google's signals; the .com is the site's address.

steps.title: Amazon AU: run the prompt and send back the tracking IDs
steps.why: The AU tags and API access are needed for per-site Amazon AU links.

steps.title: AdSense: request the DexCompare site review
steps.why: DexCompare shows no AdSense ads until Google approves the site.

steps.title: Optional: DexCompare TikTok and Threads accounts
Amazon earnings upload: on demand from /admin/earnings (download the prompt there), not a queued step
steps.why: Owner, 2026-11-03: impromptu, not weekly. The dashboard hands out a prompt with each store's dates filled in, so nothing to queue here.

steps.title: Compare Empire: apply to Commission Factory, Awin, Impact, CJ and Rakuten for the big chains' product feeds; add each approved feed URL as a GitHub secret
steps.why: Big W, Kogan, Catch, Bing Lee, Myer, David Jones, Target, Currys, Argos, AO, John Lewis, Best Buy, Walmart and the rest block server reads; their affiliate product feed is the only door, and the code already reads it (Officeworks is live without one).
